text:
maria_g: Observed a consistent small-output drift in magnet-3B int4 warmstart after very long priming (>40k tokens). Looks like punctuation flips and occasional extra whitespace. Quick repro and notes below.

maria_g: repro command (sandbox, int4 build):
```bash
./eval_runner --model magnet-3b-int4 --priming tests/long_run/repeat_sequences.txt --max-tokens 65000 --kv warmstart --seed 7
```

maria_g: example mismatch (gold vs int4 warmstart) at ~45.1k tokens:
```diff
- ... they reported 1,000,000 units.
+ ... they reported 1,000,000 units \n```

ashok: interesting, trailing space added. Is it always after a long numeric run or random words?

maria_g: pattern is biased to long numeric runs and repeated punctuation clusters ("...", "!!!"). Occurs reproducibly at same relative position across runs on same hardware. FP32 warmstart does not show it.

kevin: what build flags and runtime config?

maria_g: BUILD: QUANT=4 KERNEL_POLICY=auto ROPE_OPT=on; runtime: batch=1 seq_chunk=512 cache_prefetch=on align_pack=16

juno: could be quant pack alignment + RoPE phase wrap interaction. Have you tried align_pack=32 or disabling rope opt?

maria_g: tried align_pack=32 -> divergence shifts later (~49k). Disabling ROPE_OPT avoids divergence entirely in quick test (but performance regresses).

ashok: can you dump kv keys + per-layer phase accumulators around the event for int4 vs fp32? even a few layers might show rounding drift accumulating.

maria_g: uploading trimmed dumps to artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/magnet3b/1711119999/phase_dumps.tar.gz 

kevin: I ran a micro-harness that writes only KV writes/reads (no decode). It reproduced: the packer writes a 1-byte pad then the memcpy appears to copy extra pad into subsequent key bytes on some kernels. Running with ASAN shows a single misaligned store in quant_pack.c:line 214.

ci-bot: test-run: artifact created for #11500, magnet-3b-int4 micropack-harness, logs: https://ci.internal/runs/11500 :gear: 

juno: that points to a packing memcpy bug. But why does it only show up with warmstart and long priming? Maybe repeated rotations reuse KV memory layout patterns and amplify a tiny bit flip into tokenization differences.

maria_g: confirmed: forcing a zero-fill of padding bytes in the packer removes the divergence in the microtest and the full eval. Performance minorly impacted (~1.7% throughput).

ashok: plan: land a defensive zero-fill in packer, add an ASAN-only assertion for alignment in CI microtests, and gate ROPE_OPT for quantized warmstart until we have a proper vectorized rewrite.

kevin: I'll open a PR with the zero-fill and a targeted unit test that runs the micropack harness across sequences with long numeric runs.

maria_g: filed ticket ML-5178 with reproduction steps + links. Adding a rollout flag to prevent quantized warmstart on Dedicated until fix is validated.

juno: thanks — also add a perf benchmark so we can measure regression before/after and consider improving the packer later.

maria_g: noted. saving traces and microtest to /artifacts/magnet3b/1711119999/. Will update when PR merges.
